mcq.q: Which waste should NOT be put in a compost heap?
mcq.explanation: Plastic does not rot and spoils the compost.

mcq.q: What is the purpose of sticks at the bottom of the compost heap?
options: They keep the heap dry forever
They let air move through the heap
mcq.explanation: Air helps the tiny living things rot the wastes.

mcq.q: After about how long should the compost heap first be turned?
mcq.explanation: Turning after a few weeks gives air and mixes the heap.

mcq.q: Which is a benefit of compost to sandy soil?
options: It makes the soil more sandy
It helps the soil to hold water
mcq.explanation: Compost holds water like a sponge.

mcq.q: Why does compost help the environment?
options: It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
It uses up all the water
mcq.explanation: It turns waste into useful manure.

mcq.q: Which of these is a part of a simple drip system?
mcq.explanation: A container holds water for the pipe or bottle.

mcq.q: Who should make holes in bottle caps and pipes with a nail?
mcq.explanation: Nails and awls are sharp and can cause injuries.

mcq.q: What is the best time of day to water crops?
mcq.explanation: The sun is less hot, so less water evaporates.

mcq.q: What might happen if the water for a drip system is dirty?
mcq.explanation: Dirt gets stuck in tiny holes.

mcq.q: What could a school use to make a simple drip system?
options: A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
mcq.explanation: A bottle with small holes in its cap drips slowly.

mcq.q: Why is wet firewood a poor fuel?
options: It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
mcq.explanation: Wet wood wastes heat drying itself.

mcq.q: What should you do with the fire when cooking is finished?
mcq.explanation: Leaving fire burning wastes fuel and is dangerous.

mcq.q: Which is a problem of cutting many trees for firewood?
options: Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
mcq.explanation: Trees protect soil and water, so cutting them harms the environment.

mcq.q: What should you do after the water starts to boil?
options: Open the pot and blow on it
Turn the flame down or move wood back
mcq.explanation: A gentle flame is enough to keep the water boiling.

mcq.q: Which of these can be used to keep boiled water hot?
mcq.explanation: A flask keeps water hot so it need not be boiled again.

mcq.q: What is a scarecrow?
options: A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
mcq.explanation: A scarecrow frightens away birds and other animals.

mcq.q: Where is a scarecrow best placed?
options: In the middle or at the side of the crop where animals come from
mcq.explanation: It must be seen by the animals that come to the crop.

mcq.q: What word means living peacefully together with wild animals?
mcq.explanation: To coexist is to live together.

mcq.q: What is poaching?
options: Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
mcq.explanation: Poaching is against the law.

mcq.q: What might a hungry hare eat in a garden?
mcq.explanation: Hares nibble young plants.

mcq.q: What is direct sowing?
options: Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
mcq.explanation: The seedlings are never moved.

mcq.q: What is a seedbed?
options: The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
mcq.explanation: A seedbed is where seeds are sown.

mcq.q: How deep should tiny seeds be sown?
mcq.explanation: The smaller the seed, the shallower it should be sown.

mcq.q: Why do we cover the seeds with a thin layer of fine soil?
options: To protect them and keep them moist
mcq.explanation: Covering helps seeds germinate.

mcq.q: About how far apart should carrot plants be after thinning?
mcq.explanation: Carrots need a few centimetres to grow roots.

mcq.q: What should be done first before pulling out seedlings when thinning?
options: Water the bed so the soil is soft
mcq.explanation: Wet soil lets you pull gently without harming others.

mcq.q: Which of these is a fruit crop?
mcq.explanation: Guava is a fruit.

mcq.q: What do roots of a fruit tree do?
options: Hold the tree and take in water and food
mcq.explanation: Roots anchor and absorb.

mcq.q: Where should you buy fruit seedlings?
mcq.explanation: Good seedlings are disease-free and true to type.

mcq.q: How should the seedling be removed from its polythene bag?
options: Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
mcq.explanation: Broken roots harm the seedling.

mcq.q: What is a trellis?
options: A support structure for climbing plants
mcq.explanation: A trellis is posts and wires to hold climbers.

mcq.q: Which sign shows that a guava is ripe?
options: It is dark green and hard
It turns yellowish and smells sweet
mcq.explanation: Ripe guavas change colour and smell sweet.

mcq.q: Why should young fruit trees be watered in dry weather?
options: Their roots are small and cannot reach much water
mcq.explanation: Young trees are easily stressed by drought.

mcq.q: How far apart may passion fruit plants be planted?
mcq.explanation: Give climbers room.

mcq.q: What should be done with extra fruits?
options: Share or sell them and avoid wasting
mcq.explanation: Extra fruits can earn money or feed others.

mcq.q: Why is it best to plant fruit varieties that suit the local climate?
mcq.explanation: Wrong climate gives poor growth.

mcq.q: What is a domestic animal?
options: An animal that lives freely in the forest
An animal found only in parks
An animal kept and cared for by people
An animal that cannot be tamed
mcq.explanation: Domestic animals depend on people for food, water and shelter.

mcq.q: What is the young one of a sheep called?
mcq.explanation: A young sheep is a lamb.

mcq.q: Which product comes from a hen?
mcq.explanation: Hens lay eggs.

mcq.q: How does manure from animals help crops?
options: It supplies plant food to the soil
mcq.explanation: Manure enriches the soil.

mcq.q: Why should a poultry house be clean and dry?
options: To keep birds healthy and safe
mcq.explanation: Dirty houses spread diseases.

mcq.q: What is meant by income from animals?
options: Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
mcq.explanation: Farmers sell products to earn money.

mcq.q: Why should raw milk be boiled before drinking?
mcq.explanation: Boiling makes it safe.

mcq.q: Which of these is a body-building food?
mcq.explanation: Beans have protein.

mcq.q: What do protective foods do?
options: Help the body to fight sickness
mcq.explanation: Vitamins and minerals help protect health.

mcq.q: What does proportion mean in a meal?
options: The right amount of each kind of food
mcq.explanation: Proportion means the right amounts.

mcq.q: Which fruit is a protective food?
mcq.explanation: Mango has vitamins.

mcq.q: Which is a cheap way of getting a balanced meal?
options: Grow vegetables and fruits at home
mcq.explanation: A kitchen garden gives fresh food.

mcq.q: Which of these is an energy-giving fat?
mcq.explanation: Oils give a lot of energy.

mcq.q: What is shallow frying?
options: Cooking in a small amount of hot oil in a pan
Cooking in a lot of deep oil
mcq.explanation: Shallow frying uses a thin layer of oil.

mcq.q: Which of these is used for shallow frying?
mcq.explanation: A flat pan holds a little oil.

mcq.q: Why are eggs put in cold water after boiling?
options: To cool them so they are easy to peel
mcq.explanation: Cold water stops cooking and cools the eggs.

mcq.q: Which is an advantage of boiling?
mcq.explanation: Boiled food is low in fat.

mcq.q: Which way should pot handles point?
mcq.explanation: Handles sticking out can be knocked.

mcq.q: What should be done with a fire after cooking?
options: Put it out or switch off the gas
mcq.explanation: This prevents accidents and saves fuel.

mcq.q: Which kitchen item helps to turn food in a pan?
mcq.explanation: A spatula lifts and turns food.

mcq.q: When should you wash your hands?
options: Before eating and after using the toilet
mcq.explanation: These are key times.

mcq.q: Why is a tippy tap useful?
options: It works without a water tap and saves water
mcq.explanation: It can be made from a jerrican.

mcq.q: Which food is bad for teeth if eaten too often?
mcq.explanation: Sugar helps decay.

mcq.q: How should drinking water be stored?
options: In a clean container with a lid
mcq.explanation: Covering keeps germs out.

mcq.q: Which PPE protects the nose and mouth from dust?
mcq.explanation: A dust mask covers the nose and mouth.

mcq.q: What is the use of a hygiene log?
mcq.explanation: A log helps to form habits.

mcq.q: Which method removes dry dirt from the floor with a broom?
mcq.explanation: Sweeping uses a broom.

mcq.q: Why is a damp cloth used for dusting?
mcq.explanation: Damp cloths hold dust.

mcq.q: What is refuse?
mcq.explanation: Refuse means waste.

mcq.q: Which of these is an improvised duster?
options: A piece of clean old cloth
mcq.explanation: Old cloth makes a duster.

mcq.q: Why should food be covered in the kitchen?
options: To keep off flies, rats and cockroaches
mcq.explanation: Covered food is protected.

mcq.q: Which is the correct order for washing dishes?
mcq.explanation: Water stays cleaner longer.

mcq.q: Which PPE protects the feet from mud and water?
mcq.explanation: Gumboots are waterproof.

mcq.q: Why should PPE be cleaned?
mcq.explanation: Clean PPE is safe and lasts longer.

mcq.q: Why should rubber boots not be dried in very strong heat?
mcq.explanation: Heat damages rubber.

mcq.q: How should rubber gloves be cleaned?
options: Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
mcq.explanation: Washing with gloves on avoids touching dirt.

mcq.q: Why might wet PPE stored away cause a problem?
mcq.explanation: Moulds grow in damp places.

mcq.q: What should you do with cleaning materials afterwards?
options: Store them away from small children
mcq.explanation: Keep them safe.

mcq.q: Which is a type of tacking stitch?
mcq.explanation: Even tacking is taught in Grade 4.

mcq.q: About how long is the long stitch in long and short tacking?
mcq.explanation: The long stitch is about 2 cm.

mcq.q: How should you carry scissors?
mcq.explanation: This avoids injury.

mcq.q: How should you finish a line of tacking?
mcq.explanation: Tacking must be easy to remove.

mcq.q: How do you place pins for tacking?
mcq.explanation: Pins across the line hold the layers.

mcq.q: When is long and short tacking a good choice?
options: For long straight seams where a quick hold is enough
For hems on very slippery cloth
mcq.explanation: It is quicker.

mcq.q: Why should you tie a knot in the thread before tacking?
options: So the needle does not move
So that the thread stays in the cloth
mcq.explanation: A knot stops the thread pulling through.

short.q: Give three benefits of using compost manure on the farm.
short.answer: It feeds crops, it softens the soil and helps it to hold water, and it is cheap because it uses waste.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct benefit.

short.q: Explain how compost conserves both soil and the environment.
short.answer: It adds food to the soil and makes it firm so it is not washed easily. It reuses wastes instead of leaving them as rubbish, and it reduces the need for factory fertiliser.
short.working: 2 marks for soil, 2 marks for environment, 1 mark for a clear example.

short.q: Why should an adult make the holes in the pipe?
short.answer: Nails and awls are sharp and can hurt children.
short.working: 1 mark for sharp tools, 1 mark for safety or injuries.

short.q: Explain why drip irrigation is useful in a dry area and describe how a school could set up a system for a row of kale.
short.answer: It saves scarce water because water reaches roots directly and little is lost. For kale: raise a bucket on a stand, attach a hose along the row, close the end, ask an adult to make small holes beside each plant, fill with clean water and check that drips are slow.
short.working: 2 marks for reasons, 3 marks for set-up steps.

short.q: Explain how an improved jiko saves fuel.
short.answer: Its walls keep the heat close to the pot, so food cooks faster, and less charcoal or wood is used.
short.working: 1 mark for heat close to pot, 1 mark for faster cooking, 1 mark for less fuel.

short.q: A family boils beans for a long time on a big fire with the lid off. Suggest five ways to improve fuel use.
short.answer: Soak the beans first, cook with the lid on, use dry wood, reduce the flame after boiling starts, cut food or use an improved jiko, put out the fire after cooking.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct way.

short.q: State two safety rules when making a scarecrow.
short.answer: Ask an adult to help with sharp or heavy work; do not use wire or broken glass; wear gloves for rough poles (any two).
short.working: 1 mark for each rule.

short.q: Why is poison or a trap not a good way of dealing with wild animals?
short.answer: It can kill other animals, pets and people, it hurts animals, and it harms nature.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct reason, up to 4.

short.q: Describe how to prepare a fine seedbed in three steps.
short.answer: Clear weeds and stones; dig and loosen the soil; break the lumps with a rake until fine and level (add compost).
short.working: 1 mark for each correct step.

short.q: How can a school without land grow radish or amaranth?
short.answer: Use a box or tin with drainage holes filled with fine soil and compost; sow the seeds thinly; water gently and place in sunlight.
short.working: 1 mark each for container, sowing, care.

short.q: Name two woody fruit trees and two climbing fruit crops.
short.answer: Woody: guava, tree tomato, mango; climbing: passion fruit, grapes, kiwi, blackberry.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct example.

short.q: Describe how to make a simple trellis for passion fruit.
short.answer: Fix strong posts about 2 m tall; tie strong wires or strings between them; plant seedlings near the posts; tie the stems gently to the wires.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct step.

short.q: Why should fruit be washed before it is eaten?
short.answer: To remove dirt and germs so it is safe to eat.
short.working: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for germs or safety.

short.q: Write a plan for growing a passion fruit plant from planting to harvest.
short.answer: Build a trellis; dig and prepare a hole with compost; plant a seedling; water and mulch; tie the stem to the support; weed and prune; harvest ripe fruits and wash before eating.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

short.q: Name the young of a cow, a goat and a sheep.
short.answer: Calf, kid and lamb.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct name.

short.q: Explain the difference between domestic and wild animals.
short.answer: Domestic animals are kept and cared for by people. Wild animals live freely in nature.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct description.

short.q: Explain how domestic animals contribute to food production in a community.
short.answer: They give milk, eggs and meat directly; their manure and draught power help to grow crops; and money from sales can buy other foods.
short.working: 2 marks for direct food, 2 for crops, 1 for income.

short.q: Plan a balanced supper using local foods and name the group of each food.
short.answer: For example, rice (energy), fish (body-building), spinach (protective).
short.working: 1 mark for each food correctly named and placed.

short.q: Explain what is wrong with a meal of ugali and salt only, and how to improve it.
short.answer: It only gives energy. Add beans or fish for body-building and vegetables or fruit for protective foods.
short.working: 1 mark for problem, 1 for protein addition, 1 for protective addition.

short.q: Name three foods that can be shallow fried.
short.answer: Eggs, fish, sausages, onions, chapati (any three).
short.working: 1 mark for each food.

short.q: Describe how to shallow fry an egg.
short.answer: Crack the egg into a bowl; heat a little oil in the pan; slide the egg in; cook until the white is firm; lift out with a spatula.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four steps.

short.q: Explain how to make a meal of boiled potatoes and fried egg balanced.
short.answer: Potatoes give energy and the egg gives protein. Add vegetables such as spinach or tomato for protective foods.
short.working: 1 mark for each group named.

short.q: Describe how to wash hands correctly.
short.answer: Wet hands; use soap; rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs and nails for about 20 seconds; rinse; dry with a clean cloth.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

short.q: Name three PPE items and what each protects.
short.answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
short.working: 1 mark for each item with its use.

short.q: Explain how good personal hygiene helps prevent diseases such as diarrhoea.
short.answer: Washing hands removes germs before they reach the mouth. Safe water and clean food stop germs entering the body. Using the toilet and washing hands afterwards stops germs from spreading.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct point.

short.q: Describe how to mop a floor.
short.answer: Sweep first; fill a bucket with clean soapy water; squeeze the mop; start from the far corner and mop backwards to the door; rinse the mop; leave the floor to dry with a warning.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four steps.

short.q: Explain three safety rules when cleaning.
short.answer: Do not mix chemicals; keep chemicals from children; wear gloves for dirty work; do not leave floors wet (any three).
short.working: 1 mark for each rule.

short.q: Name three PPE items and say what each protects.
short.answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud and water; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
short.working: 1 mark for each item with its use.

short.q: How should cloth items such as overalls and cloth masks be cleaned?
short.answer: Wash with soap and water, rinse well and dry in the sun to help kill germs.
short.working: 1 mark for each part.

short.q: Plan a class display of cleaned PPE. Say what you would show and what information cards you would write.
short.answer: Display gloves, gumboots, mask, headgear, overall, canvas shoes; cards say what each protects and how to clean it; safe storage; explain to visitors.
short.working: 2 marks for items, 2 marks for cards, 1 mark for explaining.

short.q: Describe how to make long and short tacking.
short.answer: Mark a line; make a long stitch of about 2 cm on top; make a short stitch of about 0.5 cm underneath; repeat along the line; finish with a small back stitch.
short.working: 1 mark for each step.

short.q: Explain three mistakes to avoid when tacking.
short.answer: Uneven stitches, pulling the thread too tight, using thread the same colour as the cloth, making a hard knot at the end (any three).
short.working: 1 mark for each mistake.

short.q: Compare even tacking and long and short tacking. Say which is quicker and which holds more firmly.
short.answer: Even tacking is more even and holds more firmly; long and short tacking is quicker because each stitch covers more cloth.
short.working: 1 mark each for each stitch description, 1 each for quicker and firmer.
